0.x: **Later Vedic (post-Rigvedic) period = 1000–600 BC (BCE).** The texts were composed in the upper Gangetic basin.
**Course:** **Punjab → Ganga-Yamuna Doab** (Kurukshetra, Delhi, upper Doab) → **Kosala** (eastern UP), **Kashi** (Varanasi), **Videha** (north Bihar), reached by about 600 BCE.

**Kurus** = the union of the **Bharatas and Purus**; first between the Sarasvati and Drishadvati, then Delhi and the upper Doab (Kurukshetra). **Panchalas** = the middle Doab (Bareilly, Badaun, Farrukhabad).
**Kuru-Panchala** = the **centre / axis of Aryan culture** in the post-Vedic period: the Vedic texts were compiled here.
**Hastinapura** (Meerut district, UP) lies about 100 km north-east of **Delhi**, its nearest modern city.

**Videgha Madhava** (Mathava), king of Videha, lived on the **Sarasvati**; with his priest **Gautama Rahugana** he followed **Agni Vaishvanara** (the sacrificial fire) as it burnt the forests eastward.
They crossed the **Sadanira (Gandak)**; the land beyond was settled as **Videha** – read as eastward movement and agricultural colonisation by **burning and clearing forests** (fire and iron axes).
**Agastya** = the sage said to have **Aryanised South India** (he crossed the Vindhyas).
Axis of Aryan culture = **Kuru-Panchala**; Videgha Madhava's priest = **Gautama Rahugana**; river crossed = **Sadanira (Gandak)**.

1.x: **OCP** is an ill-fired red ware that leaves an **ochre colour on the fingers**; it was **christened (named) at Hastinapur by B.B. Lal (1950–52)**.

**Four wares known to the Later Vedic people:** **Red Ware** (most popular), **Black-slipped Ware**, **Black-and-Red Ware**, **Painted Grey Ware** (most distinctive). **NBPW is not** a Later Vedic ware (post-Vedic, shiny black).

r: **Grey pottery with black linear / geometric painted designs**; mainly **bowls and dishes**; deluxe tableware of the upper strata; not polished black
**Pottery of 1000–600 BC in the Gangetic plain = PGW**
About **700 sites**, mainly in the **upper Ganga basin** and the Indo-Gangetic divide (Punjab, Haryana, western UP) – not the lower Indus basin
First found at **Ahichchhatra** (excavations 1940–44); the **Hastinapur** excavation (1950–52, **B.B. Lal**) established it as a culture
**Iron weapons**, copper objects (copper possibly from **Khetri**, Rajasthan), glass, bone, semi-precious beads (trade, barter; no coins)
**Haryana** – 13-roomed mud house; pre-iron PGW with Late Harappan pottery

1.x: Early PGW (Ghaggar-Hakra, Bhagwanpura) has **no iron**; the later Doab PGW is iron-using.
Later Vedic wares exclude NBPW; PGW = upper Ganga basin, 1000–600 BC; OCP named at Hastinapur.

Iron technology about **1000–800 BCE**; common at most **PGW sites** of the Doab
Iron arrowheads and spearheads common in western UP from about 800 BCE
Iron axes and fire cleared the Gangetic forests; iron reached Kosala and Videha by the end of the period
**Earliest iron among the classic northern sites**
Iron in the **Black and Red Ware phase, before 1200 BCE**
Iron dated to about **2953 BCE** (to 3345 BCE) – now the oldest (Tamil Nadu report, Jan 2025)
Iron AMS-dated to **2172 BCE**; the earliest claim before Sivagalai

2.x: These dates push iron use far earlier than the Gangetic 1000 BCE; they say **nothing about where PGW began**.
**First metal used in India = copper** (Chalcolithic = the "copper-stone" age, Greek *khalkos* + *lithos*); iron came later.
**Krishna ayas = iron**; Sivagalai (2953 BCE) is older than Mayiladumparai (2172 BCE).

3.x: **Agriculture** became the main livelihood; the wooden ploughshare was common; ploughs were drawn by **6, 8, 12 and even 24 oxen**.

r: **Vrihi** (ritual use; rice remains of the 8th c. BCE at Hastinapur, Atranjikhera)

3.x: **Settlements:** mainly **villages** of mud-brick and wattle-and-daub houses; **burnt bricks not common**; Hastinapur and Kaushambi only proto-urban; **true towns** came in the **NBPW phase** (second urbanisation: Shravasti, Kausambi, Hastinapur).

**Crafts:** carpentry (chariots), leather, pottery, weaving (by women), copper, bronze and iron smiths; **Shresthins** = merchant groups; units of value **nishka, satamana, krishnala**; barter still the main mode.

**Andhra:** the Iron Age in Andhra = the **Megalithic culture with BRW** (Brahmagiri, Nagarjunakonda, Gudivada, Jonnawada); H.D. Sankalia: rice was first harvested in AP in the Iron Age (Megalithic) era.
**Sep 2026:** BHU opened 22 sealed boxes of 10,000+ **Rajghat** (Varanasi) artefacts; pre-NBPW pottery dates Varanasi's urban origins to about **800 BCE**.
